This is significant because Samsung also produces HBM (High Bandwidth Memory), allowing for better integration and efficiency. This move could challenge the TSMC-SK Hynix alliance and position Samsung as a comprehensive semiconductor company.
Key points to include:
1. Google is considering Samsung Foundry for producing the I/O die of their next-gen AI chip (TPU 10/Ironwood), while the main chip stays with TSMC (1.4nm).
2. Samsung will use its 2nm process for the I/O die that connects the main chip with HBM.
3. This gives Samsung an advantage because they can provide both the I/O die and HBM together, creating synergy and potentially challenging SK Hynix's position in HBM supply.
4. Samsung's ultimate goal is to become a comprehensive semiconductor company handling main chips, I/O dies, and HBM packaging, competing with TSMC and Intel.
